qs.q: A 65-year-old man with well-controlled essential hypertension develops new-onset resistant stage 2 hypertension. Which medication class commonly used for pain management should be suspected as a contributing secondary cause?
qs.e: Nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drugs can raise blood pressure by causing sodium retention and reducing the efficacy of antihypertensive therapy. Classes like statins or PPIs do not typically induce secondary hypertension.
